entries.claim: GitHub Actions Windows run 33497321898 passed all 136 selected renderer tests and all 27 platform-applicable native tests after the fixture correction. Packaging then failed before compilation because PowerShell plus pnpm exec delivered the trailing --locked to the Tauri command parser as an unsupported build option. The immediately preceding pnpm install --frozen-lockfile and cargo test --locked gates already prove both dependency locks before packaging.

A packaging-command-only successor should retain both successful locked dependency gates, remove the redundant trailing -- --locked from the Windows Tauri build invocation, rerun the same tests and build, and finish the artifact receipt without touching runtime or server code.

GitHub Actions Windows run 33496289692 passed the closed eleven-file renderer gate with 136 tests, then compiled the native crate and failed seven of 27 Rust tests in tool_selection_core because its cfg(test) fixtures use Unix absolute path literals. On Windows those literals are relative, so Inventory correctly rejects them before selection. Twenty other native tests passed, and production discovery supplies real platform-native PathBuf values.

A narrow successor should replace only Unix-literal cfg(test) fixtures in tool_selection_core with platform-native synthetic absolute paths, keep production selection code unchanged, rerun the same Windows renderer/native/build workflow and finish the cross-platform receipt.

After the conditional matchMedia jsdom polyfill removed the Windows-specific exception, the seven inherited tests/integration/App.test.tsx cases still failed because they assert the upstream provider-list and unified-skills-panel interface that the frozen 野菜 workbench intentionally replaced. In contrast, the eleven current candidate, diagnostics, configuration, service-catalog, billing and workbench test files execute 75 current-product tests successfully when explicitly selected with release and work trees excluded.

A second narrow successor should retain the test-only matchMedia correction, replace the Windows workflow's broad inherited pnpm test:unit gate with an explicit closed list of current-product Vitest files, keep the full locked Rust suite, and finish the artifact receipt without changing runtime or server behavior.

The first clean Windows 2022 internal-build run at GitHub Actions run 33494328525 installed the locked dependency graph and passed 143 renderer test files, but seven App integration cases failed before native build because jsdom does not implement window.matchMedia and the shared test setup did not provide a polyfill. The failure is confined to the test harness; no runtime source, server, database or user configuration was changed.

A narrow successor should add a standards-shaped matchMedia polyfill only to the shared jsdom setup, rerun the existing manual private Windows workflow, retain the accepted notarized universal macOS artifact, and issue a replacement cross-platform receipt without changing application runtime behavior or the server handoff.

entries.claim: The current client only registers local discovery and TCP diagnostics; configuration preview has no real model selection and account readiness is compiled unavailable.
The inspected deployed NewAPI revision exposes public pricing with usable groups and supported endpoints; its pricing_version values are source constants, not revisions of price data.

A client-only public catalog reader and tool-access preview can use bounded anonymous GETs and project no credentials or account facts. Defensive response/time/concurrency bounds are implementation limits, not claimed production capacity or service SLA. Desktop bootstrap recognition is only a contract check, never authorization.

After diagnosing the inherited WSL2 Nightly failure, the product owner authorized adapting the client CI, pushing the correction, and verifying Windows and macOS results without modifying NewAPI or publishing installers.

Run 33335919230 at commit 548d897 compiled Windows tests with native temp, then failed with c1010070 and LNK1327 when cargo re-linked under a WSL UNC TEMP. The inherited workflows also name an unregistered config atomic-write test and cc_switch_lib, while ci.yml only triggers main and the active crate is yeschoy_desktop_lib with six pure tests.
GitHub currently provides windows-2025 x64, macos-15-intel Intel, and macos-15 arm64 hosted runners for private repositories; hosted runs consume the account's Actions allowance.
GitHub workflows with workflow_call can be called by another workflow through a local ./.github/workflows/file.yml reference at the caller's commit without inheriting secrets.
野菜API is an official desktop client whose first priority includes account access, balance, recharge, and usage visibility.
The current phase changes only the desktop client; NewAPI, servers, Nginx, and production configuration remain unchanged.
Desktop authorization is first-party authorization by the 野菜API website, not direct third-party provider login inside the client.
V1 serves novice users who already installed their AI tools but do not know how to configure them; tool installation is deferred.
V1 supports Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, and DSH (DeepSeek Harness).
The model selector must show the exact model ID so users know which model they use.
V1 compares official vendor pricing with the user's actual 野菜API pricing.
The official product display name is 野菜API.
The official mainland-optimized line root is https://yeschoy.com and the Cloudflare global-acceleration line root is https://api.yeschoy.com.
The mainland-optimized and Cloudflare global-acceleration lines share the same account, API key, model availability, and pricing semantics; only the network path differs.

The default model list shows models available to the current account and compatible with the selected tool; all models may be viewed with unavailable entries disabled and explained, and a removed model is never silently substituted.

Live NewAPI responses own current account availability, exact model IDs, and actual user pricing, while a versioned first-party 野菜API model catalog owns tool compatibility, recommendations, descriptions, and sourced official pricing; the catalog ships inside the signed client until a future server distribution interface exists.

Price comparison uses CNY per one million tokens as the primary display, preserves official source currency, labels the dated comparison exchange rate as non-billing data, separates input/output/cache and tiered dimensions, preserves native units for non-token billing, and suppresses savings claims when the basis is stale or incomparable.
V1 uses a fixed comparison exchange rate rather than automatically following short-term market movements; the product owner changes it when currency movement is considered material.
The initial fixed comparison exchange rate is 1 USD = 6.75 CNY.
The desktop client compares the official-price baseline already configured in NewAPI with the current user's NewAPI price; it must not maintain a second independent numeric official-price table.

NewAPI model_ratio, model_price, and base billing expressions are always maintained as the corresponding vendor official price; all 野菜API discounts are layered separately through user group ratios or explicit special billing rules.

The desktop account login uses first-party device authorization: the client opens the system browser for website login and explicit device approval, polls for completion, never places passwords, cookies, API keys, or final session credentials in the URL, handles cancellation and expiry explicitly, and supports website-side device revocation.

Desktop device authorization codes are single-use and expire after 10 minutes; access tokens last one hour and refresh automatically; the remembered device session expires after 30 days of inactivity and has a 90-day absolute reauthorization limit; logout, website revocation, and refresh failure are explicit invalidation paths, while sensitive account actions remain on the first-party website.

Relay API keys use account-by-device-by-tool granularity. Line and model changes reuse the same tool key, repeated configuration is idempotent, another device receives different keys, and a client reinstall that cannot prove the prior device identity is treated as a new device while old keys remain until explicit revocation.

Logging out clears only the desktop account session; revoking a lost or untrusted device also revokes all relay keys belonging to that device; rotating one tool key creates and verifies the replacement before revoking the old key, with rollback on failure; deleting local tool configuration asks separately whether to revoke its remote key.

V1 keeps no persistent configuration-backup history. Before a material configuration write it creates only an encrypted temporary rollback snapshot; successful validation deletes it immediately, failure restores from it and deletes it after recovery, and a crash leaves only an unfinished-transaction snapshot for recovery on the next launch.

The desktop account session uses least privilege: it may read the current account profile, balance, usage, available models, and prices and manage only the current device's per-tool relay keys and logout. Password, email, payment data, recharge records, user groups, other devices, other-device key plaintext, and administrative settings remain website-only or inaccessible.

V1 officially supports Windows 10 22H2 x64 and Windows 11 x64, warns that Windows 10 has ended normal support, treats Windows 11 ARM64 x64-emulation as best-effort rather than officially supported, supports macOS 13 and later, and ships a Universal macOS build for Intel and Apple Silicon.

The product owner reports having an Apple developer account but has not yet confirmed whether it is an individual or organization membership or whether Developer ID and notarization permissions are ready; a Windows code-signing certificate is believed not to be currently available.
The available Apple Developer Program membership is an individual membership; a Windows code-signing certificate is still believed not to be available.

For macOS V1, the product owner accepts direct website distribution of a Developer ID-signed and notarized DMG using the existing individual membership, does not want a Mac App Store listing, and accepts that ordinary product surfaces need not display the personal legal name while technical inspection of the signing certificate may reveal the signer identity.

Windows and macOS development continue in parallel, macOS may be published first, and Windows public distribution waits for trusted signing. A 野菜API organization publisher is preferred, but the product owner accepts a personal Windows publisher identity as a fallback; unsigned or self-signed Windows packages remain internal-only.

V1 uses first-party basic operational telemetry enabled by default to discover problems early, with conspicuous notice before any upload, an easy disable control that does not affect core functionality, a strict allowed-field list, a rotating pseudonymous telemetry identifier separated from account and device authorization identity, and no automatic upload of secrets, prompts, responses, project content, complete paths, clipboard content, or raw memory dumps.

Operational events are retained for 30 days, sanitized crash events and code stacks for 90 days, irreversibly de-identified aggregate trends for 12 months, the pseudonymous telemetry ID rotates every 30 days, and the local upload queue expires after seven days. Disabling telemetry clears the local queue and may request deletion of raw historical events, while incident-specific extensions require explicit records and a deletion date.
The 野菜API desktop client will directly fork CC Switch as its technical foundation rather than creating a separate skeleton or merely extracting adapters.
The official application identifier is com.yeschoy.desktop.
The inspected NewAPI source declares existing routes for login, refresh, self, user models, top-up, pricing, and session management.
The inspected NewAPI pricing model exposes model ID, input/output/cache ratios, billing mode/expression, enabled groups, endpoint types, and a pricing version.
The inspected CC Switch source is MIT licensed and permits modification and commercial distribution while requiring preservation of the notice.
The inspected CC Switch source includes atomic file replacement and private-file mode handling for credential-bearing files.
The inspected CC Switch source has a Pi adapter that owns explicit provider entries in Pi models.json and resolves the Pi agent directory.
The inspected NewAPI pricing UI derives token input price from model_ratio multiplied by two and by a selected or available group ratio, then applies output and cache multipliers.

The inspected NewAPI pricing response structure has pricing values and a pricing version but no explicit official-source URL, official verification timestamp, or field declaring that the base value is a vendor official price.

The inspected NewAPI models.dev ratio importer selects the cheapest non-zero provider price for duplicate model names, so imported base ratios are not mechanically guaranteed to be the model vendor's own official price.
The inspected CC Switch Tauri configuration still embeds the CC Switch updater public key and update endpoints, so a fork must replace or disable them before any 野菜API release.

The inspected CC Switch Rust dependency manifest does not declare a dedicated operating-system credential-vault dependency, while provider structures and configuration projections contain API-key fields; an explicit credential-vault boundary remains new work for the 野菜API fork.

The inspected NewAPI routes expose general user-authenticated token listing, creation, update, deletion, and key-reveal operations, but do not declare a current-device-by-tool scoped desktop key contract.

The inspected NewAPI routes expose current-user usage log and statistics queries that may be reusable internally, but a stable desktop projection and reliable device, tool, and line attribution remain unverified.

The inspected NewAPI repository is distributed under GNU AGPL version 3, so copying its server implementation into the desktop fork requires separate license review rather than being treated as part of the CC Switch MIT permission.
Microsoft states that Windows 10 22H2 reached end of support on October 14, 2025.
Tauri documents that it uses Microsoft Edge WebView2 on Windows and that WebView2 is present on Windows 10 version 1803 and later, with an official runtime installer available when needed.
Tauri documents creation of a Universal macOS application binary supporting both Apple Silicon and Intel processors.

Apple permits an eligible founder or cofounder to request conversion from an individual to an organization membership and requires organization details including a D-U-N-S Number, with business documents potentially requested for verification.
Apple documents that the Account Holder can create Developer ID Application and Installer certificates for signing and notarizing Mac software distributed outside the Mac App Store.
Apple documents that an individual App Store membership uses the person's legal name as the developer name and cannot choose a different organization-style developer name.
Apple documents that Gatekeeper checks Developer ID signatures for Mac software distributed outside the Mac App Store and that notarization adds a security assessment ticket.

Microsoft documents that signed Windows downloads display the verified publisher name, unsigned and self-signed downloads receive strong SmartScreen warnings, and even a new valid OV or EV signature may show an unrecognized-app warning until reputation accumulates.

Microsoft documents that an Individual Partner Center developer account publishes under the individual's name, while a Company account publishes under a registered legal business entity, and conversion from Individual to Company is not supported.

China's Personal Information Protection Law requires clear purpose, direct relevance, minimum necessary scope, openness and transparency, prominent notice before processing, and a convenient way to withdraw consent when consent is the basis of processing.
A 2026 CAC enforcement notice identifies failures to conspicuously present collection rules before first use and collection beyond service necessity as compliance problems.
DeepSeek Harness documents a custom provider with provider ID, base URL, protocol, credential reference, and model catalog, with secrets separated from settings.yaml.

Reusing the tested CC Switch configuration adapters is likely lower risk than rebuilding every tool writer from scratch, while the account and billing experience still requires a new first-party product layer.

The target client keeps desktop sessions, per-tool relay keys, and temporary-rollback encryption keys in the operating-system credential vault and does not fall back to plaintext secret storage when that vault is unavailable.

The inspected CC Switch implementation discovers supported CLIs through the PATH-default command plus audited fallback directories, executes bounded --version probes, distinguishes not-found from installed-but-broken, and has separate Windows command-script and App Execution Alias handling.

The inspected CC Switch live writer can replace the Claude provider settings snapshot as a whole, while its Codex path contains atomic auth/config writes, exact rollback snapshots, provider-scoped bearer-token migration, and explicit official-login preservation logic. These are implementation evidence to review, not proof of the narrower 野菜API ownership and secret contract.

The inspected NewAPI snapshot registers /v1/messages and /v1/responses relay routes, and its token middleware converts an x-api-key on Claude messages or model requests into bearer authentication before token validation.

A read-only local probe on the current planning workstation found Claude Code 2.1.233 and codex-cli 0.146.0, illustrating that installed versions can lag current documentation and require explicit version gates. This is not the V1 support matrix.

Claude Code official documentation identifies ~/.claude/settings.json as the user settings file, documents CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR on Windows and other platforms, requires strict JSON, and states that the terminal and IDE surfaces read the same settings files.

Claude Code official documentation supports apiKeyHelper for dynamic credentials, documents ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and model environment variables, and ranks ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY above apiKeyHelper in credential selection.

Official OpenAI Codex configuration documentation places user provider configuration in ~/.codex/config.toml, defines custom model-provider base_url and command-backed bearer-token authentication, declares that command auth must not be combined with other credential modes, and lists responses as the only supported wire_api value.

Official OpenAI Codex authentication documentation states that login credentials may be stored in auth.json under CODEX_HOME or in the operating-system credential store, and that the CLI and IDE extension share cached login details.

Use a signed local credential helper to retrieve each tool-specific relay key from the operating-system credential vault through Claude Code apiKeyHelper and Codex model-provider command authentication; reject unsupported older tool versions instead of writing a plaintext fallback.

The product owner confirmed the Claude Code and Codex credential-helper rule: their per-tool relay keys stay in the operating-system credential vault, unsupported versions must prompt for upgrade, and the client must never fall back to plaintext key storage for compatibility.

The inspected CC Switch snapshot manages OpenCode through the exact opencode.json provider map and plugin array, parses JSON5, locks writes, and preserves unrelated top-level fields, but its provider schema permits options.apiKey and its live writer does not establish an operating-system-vault authentication plugin contract.

The inspected CC Switch snapshot manages only explicit Pi models.json.providers nodes, respects PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR, parses JSON5 with a size bound, uses content revisions and atomic private writes, preserves unrelated fields, and explicitly leaves Pi auth.json and login credentials outside its ownership. It still accepts literal provider apiKey values and does not write the selected default model.

A read-only local probe found no PATH installation for OpenCode or Pi, found DSH 0.1.0-rc.6, and observed from dsh --profile web --dump-config that the current web composition uses a credentials row named @deepseek-ai/dsh-credentials-local. This workstation observation is not a V1 support matrix.

OpenCode official documentation places the global provider configuration in ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json, stores credentials added through /connect in ~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json, supports custom OpenAI-compatible providers with baseURL and model maps, and supports top-level model and small_model selections.

The inspected OpenCode plugin API at dev commit dc4449df0d52199704ea4989a5a993ebbc605612 defines a provider authentication hook with a loader that can return runtime provider options; the official config documentation also supports loading local or package plugins. This is an extension seam, not proof that a 野菜 plugin already exists or works on a released version.

Pi official documentation at main commit 853a80d26c90a14c1886f0ebb8ffaae133ca2185 places custom providers in ~/.pi/agent/models.json, supports openai-completions and openai-responses, and resolves apiKey and header values beginning with ! by executing the command and using stdout at request time. It also documents default provider and model state separately from auth.json.

DSH official documentation at master commit cd5ef8148158c3a752a658978873241fdf8e2bbc separates credential references from settings and resolves them per operation, while the shipped local credential provider persists managed values in $DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml. The documentation explicitly leaves room for keyring- or helper-command-backed credential providers.

DSH official architecture documentation at master commit cd5ef8148158c3a752a658978873241fdf8e2bbc describes named profiles, out-of-tree plugins, profile and home cordis.patch.yml layers, row-id replacement, plugin installation through dsh plugin, and composed-config inspection through --dump-config.

For the remaining V1 tools, use a signed OpenCode auth-loader plugin, Pi's native command-backed apiKey field, and a version-pinned DSH operating-system-vault credential provider, all backed by the same local credential helper and all fail-closed without plaintext fallback.

The product owner confirmed that DSH V1 formally supports one-click configuration only for the web profile; headless, sdk, sdk-minimal, acp, and other profiles are read-only discovery targets and must not be modified in V1.

The product owner confirmed the V1 secure credential integration for the remaining tools: OpenCode uses a signed authentication plugin whose runtime loader calls the credential helper, Pi uses its native command-backed apiKey contract, and DSH uses a version-pinned operating-system-vault credential provider. Missing or incompatible security components must block configuration with no plaintext fallback.

On 2026-08-29, the latest published stable GitHub releases were Claude Code v2.1.251, Codex rust-v0.151.0, OpenCode v1.18.25, and Pi v0.84.4. The DSH repository had no GitHub Release and its newest tag was dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.1, so these versions are current research anchors rather than a verified 野菜API support matrix.

Exact-tag source inspection found the required extension seams in the current research anchors: Claude Code v2.1.251 includes recent apiKeyHelper-only gateway fixes; Codex rust-v0.146.0 through rust-v0.151.0 each include command-backed provider bearer-token schema and tests; OpenCode v1.18.25 exposes the authentication loader hook; Pi v0.84.4 documents request-time !command apiKey resolution; and DSH dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.1 exposes a credential-provider seam but explicitly ships no keyring or helper-command provider. This verifies source structure, not cross-platform 野菜API compatibility.

V1 should configure only exact tool versions that passed the complete Windows and macOS adapter matrix, with the signed client carrying the allowlist. The first verification cohort should use the three latest stable releases at test-baseline time for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and Pi, while DSH is evaluated separately against one exact prerelease tag. Unknown, newly released, and failed versions remain read-only and never receive a plaintext compatibility fallback.

entries.claim: The product owner accepted the exact-version compatibility allowlist for V1: automatic configuration is enabled only for exact tool versions that passed the complete matrix, while unknown, newly released, failed, and otherwise unverified versions remain read-only until a trusted compatibility update adds them.

The product owner rejected presenting DSH as a Developer Preview and stated that the current DSH version is materially settled. DSH web is therefore a normal V1 support target after exact-version verification, without a product preview badge; this product decision does not convert the upstream prerelease tag into an official stable release or prove compatibility before testing.

The product owner confirmed that incomplete DSH web compatibility must not block the overall V1 release. If no exact DSH version has passed the mandatory matrix at release time, DSH remains discovery-only with no configuration or credential writes until a later trusted client update adds verified support.

The product owner authorized development to begin with a governed first release unit limited to the 野菜API desktop shell, product branding, and read-only discovery and compatibility reporting for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, and DSH; account login, billing, recharge, NewAPI changes, secrets, configuration writes, automatic updates, and telemetry are excluded from this unit.

The product owner authorized the next client development unit for first-party website authorization, account balance and usage, recharge entry, and official-versus-actual price presentation while preserving the existing decision that NewAPI, servers, Nginx, and production configuration are not changed in the current phase.

The current official NewAPI GitHub HEAD 918427d8ab41f6adaa4113d0496f1f8621855b70 exposes browser login, refresh-cookie, current-user, pricing, usage-log, and top-up routes, but no /api/desktop/v1 device-authorization boundary. Its documented browser session keeps a 15-minute access token in browser memory and a rotating HttpOnly SameSite=Strict refresh cookie, so it is not a safe drop-in desktop-device credential contract.

Read-only requests to the deployed first-party origins on 2026-08-30 returned system name 野菜API and version v1.0.0-rc.27 from both /api/status endpoints, HTTP 404 for /api/desktop/v1/bootstrap, HTTP 401 for unauthenticated /api/user/self, and a public /api/pricing projection containing 37 models plus pricing_version a42d372ccf0b5dd13ecf71203521f9d2. This verifies current public behavior only and does not establish a deployed desktop authorization or stable desktop pricing projection.

RU-002 should preserve the verified RU-001 discovery experience and add a client-only account and billing shell whose sole runtime account projection is backend_upgrade_required. It must show no fabricated account, balance, usage, price, authorization, or wallet result and must make no production account request until a later frozen unit verifies the least-privilege desktop server contract.

The product owner authorized implementation to continue after RU-002 and accepted starting the next client-only one-click configuration foundation while preserving the decision not to modify NewAPI, servers, Nginx, DNS, databases, or production configuration in this phase.

The current official Codex configuration reference documents ~/.codex/config.toml, model_providers.<id>.base_url, responses-only wire_api, and model_providers.<id>.auth.command as a command that prints a bearer token to stdout; auth.command must not be combined with env_key, experimental_bearer_token, or requires_openai_auth.

The current official Claude Code documentation identifies ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL as the custom endpoint setting and apiKeyHelper as a dynamic script-based credential source, supporting a preview of owned settings without placing a literal API key in settings.

The current official OpenCode provider documentation defines custom providers under provider.<id>, uses @ai-sdk/openai-compatible for OpenAI-compatible chat-completions endpoints, accepts options.baseURL, and identifies model entries by their exact model IDs.

The current official Pi models documentation identifies ~/.pi/agent/models.json, provider baseUrl and api fields, exact model IDs, OpenAI-compatible API modes, and an apiKey value beginning with ! as a command evaluated at request time.

The locally installed official @deepseek-ai/dsh package is version 0.1.0-rc.6, points to github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness, and documents dsh web as the web-profile alias, but its public CLI documentation does not establish a stable user-owned Base URL field or a safe automatic-write adapter contract.

RU-003 should add a deterministic beginner configuration-preview planner for the fixed five-tool catalog and the two product-approved line roots. It may show only evidenced target fields and derived protocol endpoints, must leave the model ID unavailable until a server catalog exists, and must block all configuration, credential, file-read, file-write, connectivity, and rollback actions until later backend, secure-helper, and exact-version evidence is frozen.

The first governed RU-003 verification run executed five scenarios successfully but the catalog scenario failed because invoking Vitest inside the mandatory read-only source sandbox attempted to create vitest.config.ts.timestamp-*.mjs in the project root. After replacing that nested runner with direct Node TypeScript module execution, local execution passed all six scenarios; redispatch was then blocked because the dispatcher revalidated the completed RU-002 dependency against RU-003's intentionally superseding current UI outputs.

A verification-only successor release unit should preserve RU-003 product behavior and source exactly, use the corrected direct-module acceptance scenario under the mandatory read-only sandbox, retain the original failed run as historical evidence, and avoid replaying the dispatcher dependency check that compares intentionally superseded UI outputs to RU-002.

The product owner authorized one continuous goal to finish the client-side 野菜API V1 candidate without incremental approval pauses, while preserving the existing prohibition on changing NewAPI, servers, Nginx, DNS, databases, or production and without fabricating backend-dependent success.

At commit 72644de the desktop shell has truthful account and billing unavailable states, a five-tool read-only local scan, and a five-tool two-line configuration preview, but it has no home guidance destination, no line-connectivity query, no settings and security destination, bundle output is disabled, updater artifacts are disabled, and the Tauri runtime exposes only scan_tools_read_only.

Current official Tauri v2 distribution guidance supports platform-specific installers and states that direct macOS distribution requires code signing and notarization while Windows distribution provides installer and code-signing paths.
Current Apple guidance requires appropriate Developer ID signing, hardened runtime, secure timestamping, notarization review, and testing for directly distributed macOS software.

Current Microsoft guidance states that unsigned downloads can show SmartScreen warnings, may be blocked by enterprise policy or Smart App Control, and do not carry publisher reputation between versions.

Current Tauri v2 updater guidance requires signed update artifacts, keeps the verification public key in the client, and requires the signing private key only in the protected build environment; update signature verification cannot be disabled.

RU-005 should supersede RU-004 and finish the bounded client-side V1 candidate by adding a guided home, user-triggered secret-free DNS and TCP-443 diagnostics for only the two approved line hosts, a settings and security truth surface, complete multilingual page states, candidate bundle configuration, and platform and backend handoff checklists while login, models, prices, credentials, configuration writes, retained backups, telemetry upload, signed updates, and production release remain unavailable.
Owner accepts the revised look and requires plain end-user wording throughout the installed desktop app, without engineering or release-audit commentary.

The deployed NewAPI status endpoint currently returns usd_exchange_rate 1 and quota_per_unit 500000 on both lines, and its desktop-session allowlist permits the token list, create, reveal, update and delete routes needed by a native-only setup transaction.

The command reuses or creates one dedicated unrestricted tool token per target, validates the selected account model and compiled origin, writes only owned fields with transaction-scoped in-memory rollback, returns no credential or path, and retains no backup history.
